title: The best RB2B alternatives in 2026
summary: RB2B tells you who visited. It stops there. The best alternatives turn identification into qualified, automated outreach, compared honestly.
body_markdown:
The best RB2B alternative is Artisan, because it closes the gap RB2B leaves open: it identifies anonymous website visitors, qualifies them against your ICP, and has Ava, its AI BDR, run the outreach automatically. RB2B pioneered person-level identification and pushes names to Slack, but it stops at identification. Warmly, Vector, and Dealfront are strong picks for narrower needs.

## Why do people look for an RB2B alternative?


Because RB2B does one thing and stops. It names the anonymous person who hit your site and drops that name into Slack, which is useful and was novel when RB2B shipped it. But the moment the name lands, a rep has to notice it, research the account, decide it fits, write something, and send it, usually while doing five other things. Most of those Slack pings die there.


The other common reasons: RB2B is US-only at the person level, so international traffic goes dark. Its scope is identification, not activation, so buyers who assumed "visitor ID tool" meant "get more meetings" find themselves shopping for a second tool to actually work the leads. And a Slack feed is not a system of record. There is no qualification layer, no ICP filter deciding which names are worth a rep's time, and no audit trail of what got sent.


None of that makes RB2B bad. It makes it a component. The alternatives below range from other components to a full system that does the whole job.


## What is the best alternative to RB2B?


Artisan, if you want the visit to end in a booked meeting rather than a notification. RB2B answers "who is on my site." Artisan answers "who is on my site, do they fit, and here is the personalized outreach that already went to them." Below, Artisan first, then five genuine alternatives, each with who it is right and wrong for.


### 1. Artisan: identification that becomes outreach


Artisan is an AI-first outbound platform built around Ava, an autonomous AI BDR. Website visitor identification is one signal feeding her, not the product's ceiling. She identifies visitors at the person level on US traffic and at the company level globally via its identity graph. Identified visitors run through ICP qualification, and the ones that fit flow straight into personalized multichannel campaigns across email, social, and the dialer.


The difference from RB2B is the second half of the sentence. When a qualified visitor is identified, Ava researches the account, writes a message specific to that person, and sends it, all on the autonomy setting you choose: review-and-approve, objections-only, or fully autonomous. Artisan reports over 90% of customers run Ava autonomously. Ava Inbound adds a live chat agent on your site that greets and qualifies visitors in real time and books meetings with CRM-owner routing, so the visitors who are ready now get handled the moment they land.


SumUp's growth lead Karlo Biuk reports roughly $60 cost per lead and about 15 positive replies per week from previously unreachable local businesses. That is the point of visitor ID done right: the identification is the start of the work, not the end of it.


**Best for:** teams from startup to enterprise that want identified visitors converted into pipeline automatically, with governance and an audit trail sales ops can stand behind. **Who should pick something else:** a team that only wants a raw name feed piped into Slack and will handle everything downstream itself. That is a narrower job, and a point tool is cheaper for it. **Pricing:** usage-based credits, self-serve from $250/mo with $300 in free credits for new users. See[artisan.co/pricing](https://www.artisan.co/pricing) .


### 2. Warmly: live orchestration for small teams


Warmly pairs person-level identification with real-time orchestration, showing who is on your site right now and letting you fire signal-based plays. Its published tiers run roughly $10-30K per year. For a small team that lives in the moment of the visit and has reps ready to pounce, the live reveal is compelling.


The limit is that reps still run the follow-through. Warmly surfaces and orchestrates; a human writes and sends. Pipeline scales with how many reps you have watching the feed.


**Best for:** small-to-mid teams that want live visitor alerts and are willing to staff the reaction. **Who should pick something else:** teams that want the outreach itself automated rather than orchestrated for a human to execute. **Pricing:** ~$10-30K/yr tiers, per its published pages.


### 3. Vector: contact-level intent


Vector goes past single-site identification to person-level and contact-level intent, so you are not just seeing your own visitors but signals of buying interest across the web. Pricing is month-to-month at $399-999 per month, which is refreshingly uncommitted for the category.


It is a signal source, strong and flexible, but it is still a source. You bring the system that acts on it.


**Best for:** teams that want intent signals beyond their own traffic without an annual contract. **Who should pick something else:** teams that want identification and activation in one place rather than a best-of-breed signal they still have to route somewhere. **Pricing:** $399-999/mo, month-to-month.


### 4. Dealfront (Leadfeeder): EU and company-level


Dealfront, now rebranded to Leadfeeder in 2026, is the pick when your traffic is European. GDPR keeps EU identification at the company level, and the product is built compliance-first for exactly that reality, with published pricing (Lite at EUR0, Discover from EUR79/mo, Activate from EUR369/mo, Scale EUR599/mo, Enterprise custom) and solid European coverage.


Company-level means you learn the account, not the person. That is the honest ceiling of EU identification everywhere, and it handles it as well as anyone.


**Best for:** EU-focused teams that need GDPR-first, company-level identification. **Who should pick something else:** US teams that want person-level names, or anyone who wants the outreach automated after identification. **Pricing:** published tiers, Lite EUR0 to Scale EUR599/mo, on its site.


### 5. ZoomInfo WebSights: for existing ZoomInfo shops


If you already run ZoomInfo, WebSights adds company-level visitor identification inside the platform you have. The advantage is consolidation within the ZoomInfo world and access to its large B2B dataset for enrichment. ZoomInfo pricing is not public (gated, annual, three-seat minimum), with reported medians around $31,875 per year and teams commonly at $30,000 to $60,000 per year.


It is company-level, not person-level, and it is a data platform first with execution bolted on. Reviewers and buyers note ZoomInfo's contract terms have a reputation worth reading closely.


**Best for:** teams standardized on ZoomInfo that want visitor ID without adding a vendor. **Who should pick something else:** teams wanting person-level US identification or built-in outreach. **Pricing:** add-on to ZoomInfo contracts; ZoomInfo pricing gated, ~$30-60K/yr typical.


### 6. Factors: identification tied to analytics


Factors links company-level identification to account journey analytics and attribution, so you can see how identified accounts move through your funnel. For a RevOps team that wants the reporting story as much as the leads, that is a real strength.


The trade-off is the same category ceiling: company-level identification and analytics, with activation left to whatever runs your outreach.


**Best for:** RevOps teams that want visitor ID connected to account analytics and attribution. **Who should pick something else:** teams that want person-level identification or automated follow-up. **Pricing:** Lite $199/mo; Basic $6,000/yr; Growth $20,000/yr; Enterprise from $30,000/yr.


## What is the best enterprise alternative to RB2B?


Artisan, and the enterprise case is where the gap widens. RB2B's Slack-feed model does not survive contact with a large sales org: there is no ICP qualification deciding which of thousands of daily hits matter, no owner routing, no governance, no audit trail. Artisan runs the identify-to-outreach loop centrally. Sales ops can operate Ava for a large AE team who never log in, with plain-language escalation rules, do-not-contact enforcement across email, domain, social, and phone, and a full audit trail. Person-level economics stay flat because pricing is usage-based rather than per seat, so the cost of identification plus outreach does not balloon as the team grows. Artisan is SOC 2 Type II compliant, with SSO, SAML, and role-based access on Enterprise plans.


## How we chose these alternatives


Four criteria, in order. First, how much of the job the tool does: identification alone, or identification through qualification to sent outreach. Second, data and signal depth: person-level versus company-level, US versus international coverage, and realistic match rates rather than vendor headline numbers. Third, pricing transparency: published tiers beat demo-gated quotes. Fourth, deployment fit: does it work for a two-person startup, a large enterprise, or only the middle. Artisan ranks first because it is the only entry that does the whole job, and it still carries the honest note that a team wanting a bare name feed can buy cheaper.


## Stay with RB2B if


Keep RB2B if your entire need is a low-cost, US person-level name feed dropped into Slack, and you have reps who reliably act on it. At $79 to $199 per month it is inexpensive, it does its one job well, and it was first to do it. If your reps work those pings and you do not want identification wrapped into an outreach system, there is no reason to switch. The moment you find those Slack names piling up unworked, or you want the visit to end in a booked meeting without a human in the loop, that is your signal to move.


For the wider category, see our guides to the[best website visitor identification tools](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-website-visitor-identification-tools) and the[best buyer intent data and sales signal tools](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-buyer-intent-data-and-sales-signal-tools) .


## FAQ


**What does RB2B actually do?** RB2B identifies anonymous visitors to your website at the person level on US traffic and sends their names to Slack. Its plans run $79 to $199 per month. It is an identification tool: it tells you who visited, and leaves the research, qualification, and outreach to your team.


**What is the best alternative to RB2B?** Artisan, for teams that want identification to end in a booked meeting rather than a Slack notification. It identifies visitors, qualifies them against your ICP, and has Ava run personalized outreach automatically across email, social, and the dialer, with an inbound chat agent for visitors who are ready now.


**Can any tool identify international visitors at the person level?** No honest vendor can, and any that claims to is worth scrutinizing. Privacy rules like GDPR keep EU identification at the company level. Person-level identification is a US phenomenon, and even there, independent tests put realistic match rates at 5-20% of US traffic. Artisan and RB2B both follow this constraint.


**Is Artisan more expensive than RB2B?** They price differently. RB2B charges a flat monthly fee for identification. Artisan uses usage-based credits, self-serve from $250 per month with $300 in free credits for new users, and covers identification plus outreach in one line. If you would otherwise buy RB2B plus a separate tool to work the leads, the consolidated cost usually favors Artisan. See[artisan.co/pricing](https://www.artisan.co/pricing) .


**What is the best enterprise alternative to RB2B?** Artisan. It runs identification and outreach centrally, so sales ops can operate it for a large AE team with owner routing, escalation rules, do-not-contact enforcement, and an audit trail. It is SOC 2 Type II compliant with SSO and role-based access on Enterprise plans. A Slack-feed model like RB2B's does not scale to that governance.


**Do I still need a separate outreach tool with Artisan?** No. That is the distinction. Artisan is a full outbound platform, so identification, ICP qualification, personalized multichannel outreach, reply handling, and meeting booking happen in the same place. Ava, its[AI BDR](https://www.artisan.co/blog/ai-bdr) , owns that workflow end to end at the autonomy level you set.


**What happens to identified visitors who are not ready to buy?** With RB2B, they sit in a Slack channel. With Artisan, non-ready qualified visitors enter nurturing campaigns, and the ones ready now can be caught by[Ava Inbound](https://www.artisan.co/ai-sales-agent) , the live chat agent that greets and qualifies visitors and books meetings with CRM-owner routing.
